questions.question: A fraction bar shows one whole granola bar cut into 8 equal parts. Emma shades 3 of those parts. Which choice correctly names the shaded amount of that one whole bar?
options: 3/8, because 3 of the 8 equal parts of this one bar are shaded
3/16, because you count the 8 parts on this bar and the 8 parts on the bar beside it
3 out of 8 parts, whether or not the 8 parts are the same size
3/5, because 3 parts are shaded and 5 parts are not shaded
questions.explain: A fraction names equal parts of ONE whole: the bottom number is how many equal parts the whole bar was cut into (8) and the top number is how many are shaded (3), so it is 3/8. The usual trap is counting the leftover parts (3 and 5) or dragging in a second bar — the whole is just this one bar.

questions.question: A ribbon is one whole. It is cut into 4 pieces, but the pieces are not the same length — two long pieces and two short pieces. One short piece is coloured. Which statement about the coloured piece is correct?
options: It is 1/4 of the ribbon, because the ribbon was cut into 4 pieces
It is not 1/4 of the ribbon, because the 4 pieces are not equal parts of the whole ribbon
It is 1/4, because a different ribbon cut into 4 equal parts also has 1/4 coloured
It is 1/2 of the ribbon, because it is one of the two short pieces
questions.explain: Fraction names like 1/4 only work when the one whole is cut into EQUAL parts, so uneven pieces cannot be called fourths. The common trap is just counting pieces — 4 pieces does not mean fourths unless every piece is the same size.

questions.question: Bar A is one whole paper strip 12 cm long, cut into 3 equal parts, with 1 part shaded. Bar B is one whole paper strip 24 cm long, also cut into 3 equal parts, with 1 part shaded. Which statement is true?
options: Bar A shows 1/3 but Bar B shows 2/3, because Bar B is twice as long
1/3 of Bar B is a bigger fraction than 1/3 of Bar A, because Bar B is longer
Each bar has 1/3 of its own whole shaded, so the fractions are the same even though the shaded lengths are different
Neither bar shows 1/3, because the two bars are not the same length
questions.explain: A fraction always describes its own whole: 1 of 3 equal parts is 1/3 no matter how long the strip is, even though 1/3 of 24 cm (8 cm) is longer than 1/3 of 12 cm (4 cm). The trap is thinking a longer bar makes the fraction itself bigger — the amount changes, the fraction does not.

questions.question: One whole chocolate bar is cut into 6 equal parts and 5 parts are shaded, so the shaded amount is 5/6. What does the 6 tell you?
options: How many pieces there are, even if the pieces are different sizes
How big the whole chocolate bar is
How many parts there are on this bar and on the bar beside it added together
How many equal parts the one whole bar was cut into
questions.explain: The denominator counts the EQUAL parts that one whole was cut into, and the numerator counts how many of them are taken. The trap is counting pieces of any size, or counting parts from more than one whole — both break the meaning of the fraction.

questions.question: Liam writes 1/2 = 2/4. Which explanation shows why these are equivalent fractions?
options: Because splitting each half of the SAME one whole into 2 equal parts gives 4 equal parts, and 2 of them cover exactly the same amount
Because you can cut any shape into 4 pieces of any size and shade 2 of them
Because half of a small juice box is the same as two quarters of a large juice box
Because 1 + 1 = 2 and 2 + 2 = 4, so the fractions match
questions.explain: Equivalent fractions name the same amount of the same one whole, cut into more (or fewer) equal parts — split each half in two and you get 2 of 4 equal parts. The traps are switching to a different-sized whole partway through, or just playing with the numbers.

questions.question: Maya has a 500 mL water bottle and Noah has a 1 L water bottle. At soccer practice Maya drinks 3/4 of her bottle and Noah drinks 3/4 of his bottle. Which statement is correct?
options: They drank the same amount of water, because 3/4 equals 3/4
Both fractions are 3/4, but they describe different wholes, so Noah drank more water
Maya drank more water, because 3/4 of a small bottle is a bigger fraction
Noah drank 6/8 of a bottle, which is a larger fraction than Maya's 3/4
questions.explain: Equal fractions only mean equal amounts when the whole is the same: 3/4 of 1000 mL is 750 mL but 3/4 of 500 mL is only 375 mL. The trap is comparing 3/4 with 3/4 and forgetting to ask '3/4 of what whole?' (and 6/8 is just another name for 3/4, not a bigger fraction).

questions.question: You want to show on one whole fraction strip that 2/3 and 4/6 are equivalent. What should you do?
options: Cut the strip into 6 pieces of any size you like and shade 4 of them
Draw a second, longer strip, cut it into 6 parts, and shade 4 of them
Split each of the 3 equal parts of that same strip into 2 equal parts, making 6 equal parts, and shade 4
Add 2 to the top number and 3 to the bottom number, since 2 + 2 = 4 and 3 + 3 = 6
questions.explain: To show equivalence you re-cut the SAME whole into smaller equal parts — each third becomes 2 sixths, so 2/3 covers exactly the same strip as 4/6. The traps are using a different-sized strip or making pieces that are not equal, because then neither name is a true fraction of that whole.

questions.question: Ava wants to check whether 3/6 and 1/2 are equivalent. Which check actually works?
options: Compare 3 of the 6 pieces of a strip that was torn into uneven pieces with 1 of 2 equal parts
Compare 3 of 6 equal parts of a 30 cm strip with 1 of 2 equal parts of a 10 cm strip
Compare only the top numbers: 3 is more than 1, so 3/6 must be more than 1/2
Compare 3 of 6 equal parts with 1 of 2 equal parts of the same whole strip
questions.explain: A fair check keeps ONE whole and cuts it into equal parts both ways — 3 of 6 equal parts covers the same strip as 1 of 2 equal parts, so they are equivalent. The traps are using two different-sized strips or uneven pieces, which makes the comparison meaningless before you even start.

questions.question: At a Burnaby bake sale there are two trays of brownies, both the same width. The large tray is 40 cm long and the small tray is 20 cm long. Jayden eats 1/4 of the large tray and Priya eats 1/2 of the small tray. Who ate more brownie?
options: They ate the same: 1/4 of 40 cm is 10 cm and 1/2 of 20 cm is 10 cm, because the two fractions describe different wholes
Priya, because 1/2 is greater than 1/4
Jayden, because his tray is bigger, so any fraction of it must be bigger
You cannot tell, because 1/4 and 1/2 are not equivalent fractions
questions.explain: Work out the amount each fraction stands for on its own whole first: 1/4 of 40 cm is 10 cm and 1/2 of 20 cm is 10 cm, so the two servings are equal. The classic trap is comparing 1/4 with 1/2 straight away — fractions can only be compared like that when they come from the same whole.

questions.question: Owen cuts one rectangular birthday cake into 3 pieces: one big piece and two smaller pieces. He hands his sister a small piece and says 'You got 1/3 of the cake.' Which reply is correct?
options: He is right — the cake was cut into 3 pieces, so every piece is 1/3
He is wrong — a piece is 1/3 only when the whole cake is cut into 3 EQUAL parts, so her smaller piece is less than 1/3
He is right, because 1/3 of the small piece is the same as 1/3 of the big piece
He is wrong — her piece is 1/2, because there are two small pieces
questions.explain: Thirds means the one whole cake is shared into 3 parts of the same size, so uneven pieces cannot be named 1/3 at all — her small piece is less than a real third. The trap is counting pieces instead of checking that the parts are equal.

questions.question: A community garden in Kelowna has two beds. Class A's bed is 12 m long and they plant carrots in 3/4 of it. Class B's bed is 8 m long and they plant carrots in 3/4 of it. A parent says 'Both classes planted the same fraction, so both planted the same number of metres.' Which reply is correct?
options: Right — both fractions are 3/4, so both classes planted the same number of metres
Wrong — Class B planted a bigger fraction, because 3/4 of a smaller bed means bigger parts
Wrong about the metres — 3/4 of 12 m is 9 m and 3/4 of 8 m is 6 m; the fraction is the same but the wholes are different
Wrong — 3/4 of the 8 m bed is really 6/8, so it is a different fraction from 3/4
questions.explain: Split each bed into 4 equal parts and take 3: 12 m gives 3 m parts (9 m planted) and 8 m gives 2 m parts (6 m planted), so the same fraction covers different lengths. The trap is treating 3/4 as a fixed amount instead of asking '3/4 of which whole?' (6/8 is just another name for 3/4, not a different fraction).

questions.question: Ella and Ben each get a 30 cm ribbon strip for art class — the strips are exactly the same length. Ella cuts hers into 6 equal parts and uses 4 of them. Ben cuts his into 3 equal parts and uses 2 of them. Ben says 'I used less ribbon, because I only used 2 pieces.' What is true?
options: You cannot compare them, because Ella's pieces and Ben's pieces are not the same size
Ben used less, because 2 pieces is fewer than 4 pieces
Ben used less, because his ribbon was cut into fewer parts, so his whole is smaller
They used the same amount: 4 of 6 equal parts and 2 of 3 equal parts of the same 30 cm whole are both 20 cm
questions.explain: Find the size of each part first: Ella's parts are 5 cm (4 x 5 = 20 cm) and Ben's are 10 cm (2 x 10 = 20 cm), so 4/6 and 2/3 name the same amount of the same 30 cm whole. The trap is counting pieces instead of measuring — more pieces just means smaller equal parts, not more ribbon.
